source.title: IN14: Post-hearing advice
source.publisher: Planning Inspector / London Borough of Enfield examination library

facts.finding: Land at Chase Park South requires an accurate inset map for developable area and Green Belt boundary; policy should be clear development is not intended within the SINC.

Arnold House & Land to the rear should make clear that development is not intended within the SINC and any related routes/green infrastructure require assessment and mitigation of SINC/woodland impacts.
Chase Park North East criteria require stronger mandatory wording and clarity on the purpose of the buffer.
Chase Park North West should align with Policy PL10 and include a suitable buffer to Trent Park.
Chase Park policy requires clearer acceptable density guidance.
Chase Park policy should clearly address a suitable Trent Park buffer and its purpose.
Chase Park policy requires clear transport impact minimisation/mitigation and capacity wording.
Biodiversity mitigation wording should be strengthened; school playing fields in the SINC should only be contemplated without unacceptable biodiversity impact.
Land between Camlet Way and Crescent Way is a highly sensitive Green Belt/AoSC location bordering Hadley Wood Conservation Area and a SINC.
Inspector was not persuaded benefits outweighed Green Belt/character harm and found exceptional circumstances for Green Belt removal had not been demonstrated.
Inspector directed the Council to draft modifications deleting the site from the Plan and reintegrating the land into the Green Belt.
Land east of Junction 24 was not considered soundly based and would cause a very high degree of Green Belt harm.
Inspector found exceptional circumstances for this allocation had not been identified and directed deletion with consequential Green Belt/Policies Map changes.
Land at Picketts Lock allocation was included among Green Belt allocations the Inspector directed the Council to delete.
Whitewebbs Golf Course / Tottenham Hotspur Training Ground allocation was included among Green Belt allocations the Inspector directed the Council to delete.
Sloeman's Farm allocation was included among Green Belt allocations the Inspector directed the Council to delete.
Inspector concluded the policies as drafted were ineffective and not capable of being made effective through modification; deletion did not determine any separate planning permission outcome.
Inspector found allocation RAG ratings ineffective and directed their removal.
PTAL ratings may have become out of date during examination; modifications should ensure up-to-date values and tell applicants to check latest information.

facts.reference: SA1.6, SA7.3, SA7.5, URB.04, URB.05, URB.06, URB.31, URB.35
facts.finding: Council identified these allocations as fully implemented; Inspector said retaining completed allocations serves no particular purpose and they should be deleted from the Plan.
Inspector said URB.34 should be deleted as an individual allocation; the Policies Map should instead identify the site as LSIS.
Brimsdown Sports Ground allocation was considered sound in principle, while capacity should be updated to the most recent accurate position.
Albany Leisure Centre had no realistic prospect of becoming available/delivered during the plan period; continued allocation was not justified and should be deleted.
Inspector's June 2026 advice remains without prejudice to final MM decisions; Council must prepare Main Modifications for consultation before the Inspector finalises the report.
